Controlling & Quality Assurance

Control and quality assurance — standards, indicators, audit, incident reporting and stress management.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the process of control
  • List quality assurance activities in nursing
  • Explain audit and incident reporting
  • Describe evidence-based practice

In simple words

Controlling compares what was planned with what actually happened and corrects the gap. In nursing this is quality assurance: standards, audits and indicators.

Steps of control

  1. Set standards — high quality care and records
  2. Measure performance — counts, indicators, observation
  3. Compare with the standard
  4. Correct deviations
  5. Follow up and re-evaluate

Quality assurance in nursing

Activity Purpose
Nursing audit Checks whether records meet standards
Peer review Colleagues assess care against standards
Patient satisfaction survey Voice of the patient
Outcome indicators Clinically, falls, pressure ulcers, infection and mortality
Structural indicators Staffing, equipment, facilities

Incident reporting

  • Medication errors, falls, needle stick, equipment failure
  • Report within the shift, with facts and no blame
  • Data are used for learning, not punishment
  • Blame-free reporting increases safety

🔴 Evidence-based practice keeps care current

Nursing practice is corrected against evidence and current standards, not habit. Guidelines, checklists and audits make the standard visible and measurable.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Control steps: standards, measure, compare, correct, follow up.
  2. Quality assurance uses audit, peer review, satisfaction survey and outcome indicators.
  3. Incident reporting is blame-free and immediate.
  4. Audit compares records with standards.
  5. Continuous improvement follows Plan-Do-Check-Act.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Outcome indicators include falls, pressure ulcers and healthcare-associated infection.
  2. Peer review improves practice without blame.
  3. Patient satisfaction surveys capture the patient’s experience.
  4. Care pathways and protocols make practice consistent.
  5. Leadership supports staff who report incidents.

📌 Memory trick

Quality: Q-A-A-I — Quality norms, Audit, Action on gaps, Indicator follow-up.

60-second revision

  • Control: standards, measure, compare, correct, follow up.
  • Quality assurance: audit, peer review, indicators and patient satisfaction.
  • Incident reporting: blame-free, facts and immediate.
  • Evidence-based practice corrects habit.
  • PDCA drives continuous improvement.

Test yourself

Controlling focuses on:

Answer: B. Control compares actual performance with standards and corrects deviations.

A nursing audit compares care with:

Answer: B. An audit compares what was done with the agreed standard to find and fix gaps.

Which is an outcome indicator?

Answer: B. Falls rate, pressure ulcers and infections are nursing outcome indicators.

Incident reporting should be:

Answer: A. Reporting is immediate, factual and blame-free so that systems can be corrected.

The PDCA cycle stands for:

Answer: A. PDCA (Deming) is Plan-Do-Check-Act, used for continuous quality improvement.
